  2. Avoid saying phrases like “we want to terminate the contract” or “we do not want to continue with this build” as this could be considered repudiation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant acknowledges the key takeaways regarding repudiation of a building contract.
- [FACT] Repudiation of a contract occurs when a party shows an unwillingness or inability to perform substantial obligations under the contract, often referred to as renunciation.
- [FACT] Contract repudiation is considered a breach of contract, allowing the other party to terminate the contract and seek damages.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant acknowledges the explanation of what constitutes repudiation of a contract.
- [FACT] A party may breach a contractual provision, but repudiation often arises from breaches of the contract.
- [FACT] The innocent party may rely on common law right of repudiation to terminate the contract even if there is no contractual right to do so.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant acknowledges the explanation of the relationship between repudiation and breach of contract.
- [FACT] Repudiation is not the same as termination; it refers to the conduct that gives the innocent party the right to terminate the contract.
- [FACT] The innocent party may notify the party whose conduct is repudiatory to rectify the conduct before terminating the contract.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant acknowledges the distinction between repudiation and termination.
- [FACT] Accepting repudiation allows the innocent party to terminate the contract, which is deemed void at common law.
- [FACT] One cannot sue specifically for repudiation but can bring a claim for breach of contract.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant acknowledges the implications of accepting repudiation.
- [FACT] There is no straightforward formula for proving a repudiatory breach; it must be considered in context.
- [FACT] The party intending to terminate for repudiation should provide opportunities for the at-fault party to rectify the breach.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant acknowledges the complexities involved in proving a repudiatory breach
